material_scope_clarifications: The +16.2% versus +2.8% bloat comparison is a direct with-governance versus without-governance comparison in Table 6, while the -7.1-point RegR change is only the within-SkillEvo decline from 28.2% to 21.1% across rounds. Table 5 does not report a no-governance RegR comparator, so the -7.1-point trend alone is not a single-factor causal governance ablation.

The paper separates simulator-side intent coverage from agent-side exposed-intent accuracy at the metric/responsibility level, but it does not use independent model families for User Agent versus Verifier: User Agent, Verifier, Attributor, and Governor all use minimax-m3. The explicit model-family independence is Generator (Skill Editor: deepseek-v4-pro) versus Evaluator-side components (minimax-m3).

An untouched evaluation split is explicitly present: tickets are chronologically quartered per Skill, the first three quarters drive evolution, and the fourth is held out, fed back into no loop stage, and used only for measurement/reporting; version selection uses the development set.

A human-confirmation promotion gate is explicitly present: the paper states that no revision reaches production without human confirmation and the architecture lists human confirmation before production rollout.

No author-linked public code repository is linked from the checked arXiv record/HTML, and a bounded GitHub repository-name search for 'SkillEvo Tencent' returned no repositories. This is not proof that no official artifact exists elsewhere.

contradiction_check.notes: The primary paper supports the numerical claims and the held-out/human-confirmation safeguards. The important corrections are that RegR=-7.1 points is not itself a no-governance factorial, and simulator-versus-verifier independence is logical/metric separation rather than distinct model-family separation.
